dataSource.fetchedBy: research agent, verified against the official source
dataSource.notes:
SOURCE: Qdoba's own "Nutrition Facts 2026" PDF (file Nutrition_8.5.26.pdf, i.e. revised 2026-08-05 — current as of retrieval), linked as the "NUTRITION" download from https://www.qdoba.com/nutrition-allergens. The PDF is served from Qdoba's Contentful CDN (assets.ctfassets.net), which is why sourceUrl is a ctfassets.net host rather than qdoba.com — it is still Qdoba's own published document, reached only by following the link on their official nutrition page. www.qdoba.com itself is behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to non-browser fetches; I loaded the nutrition page in a real browser to obtain the current PDF link, then downloaded and text-extracted the PDF directly (pypdf).

PORTION BASIS: Every number is per one of the stated serving, exactly as the PDF lists it — most rows are direct published values. The two internally inconsistent rows called out below use labeled estimates so the calculator does not preserve values known to be impossible. The PDF's column order is: Allergens, Serving Size (g), Calories, Calories from Fat, Total Fat, Saturated Fat, Trans Fat, Cholesterol, Total Carbohydrate, Dietary Fiber, Sugar, Protein, Sodium, Potassium. I mapped Total Fat / Total Carbohydrate / Protein and validated the mapping by Atwater cross-check (cal ~= 4C + 4P + 9F) on ~35 rows; all reconciled within normal rounding/fiber tolerance except the items called out below.

WHERE THE SOURCE LISTS TWO SIZES, I kept one canonical unit and let the app's portion mechanics cover the other: guacamole, Three Cheese Queso and Queso Diablo use the 2 oz scoop (the 4 oz rows are exact 2x, and `dips` caps at 3 scoops); chorizo uses 3.0 oz and bacon 2 oz (the 1.5 oz / 1 oz rows are exact halves, covered by the split-base half-portion rule).

KNOWN SOURCE DEFECTS, corrected with labeled estimates where a useful value can be recovered:
1. Salsa Verde (1 oz) is published with Total Carbohydrate 0 g but Dietary Fiber 1 g — internally impossible. Loadout estimates 2 g carbohydrate from the 10-calorie total and the published 1 g fiber, and labels the row estimated.
2. Seasoned Potatoes (2 oz) is published as 100 cal with 12 C / 1 P / 0 F; those macros only account for ~52 cal. Their own "Calories from Fat" column is also 0, so there is no fat figure to recover. Loadout estimates 5 g fat from the unexplained energy residual and labels the row estimated.
3. Brisket Birria (3.5 oz) has "Calories from Fat" printed as 140, equal to its total calories — a typo — but its Total Fat of 7 g is consistent with the 140 cal total, so the macros I use are sound.

SIGNATURE EATS AS ENTREES: The `entrees` category holds Qdoba's published complete named entrees at their exact published totals. These are whole meals, not counter stations — they are included because the macros are fully official and directly loggable. They should NOT be combined with build-your-own components (that would double count).

PRESETS ARE INTENTIONALLY EMPTY — see the reasoning: Qdoba publishes the TOTALS for its Signature Eats but nowhere publishes the component/portion breakdown of any of them. I attempted reconciliation and it does not converge. Example: Keto Bowl - Chicken (published 340 g / 400 cal / 26 F / 11 C / 33 P); chicken + shredded cheese + guac + sour cream sums to 212 g / 430 cal / 34 F / 28 P — wrong on weight, fat and protein. Example: Chicken Queso Bowl (published 468 g / 750 cal / 33 F / 74 C / 43 P); the closest plausible build (rice + black beans + chicken + 4 oz queso + pico) gives 695 cal and no arrangement of published line items lands on 750/33/74/43. The signature builds evidently use in-house portions that differ from the standard line-item servings. Double Protein Bowl - Chicken is the one partial exception — its published cholesterol of 180 mg is exactly 2x the 90 mg of a 3.5 oz chicken portion, confirming double chicken — but the remainder still misses by ~10 cal / 2 g fat / 2 g protein, which is a real defect for a macro app. Rather than ship a component list Qdoba never published and that fails the sum check, I returned zero presets, per the brief's explicit allowance. If presets are wanted later, the honest path is Qdoba's in-app ordering builder, not this PDF.

items.name: Seasoned Potatoes
items.notes: Estimated fat: Qdoba's August 2026 guide publishes 100 calories, 12 g carbohydrate, 1 g protein, and 0 g fat, but the stated macros account for only 52 calories. The remaining energy implies about 5.3 g fat; rounded to 5 g. Calories, carbohydrate, and protein remain the official values. Medium confidence.

items.name: Salsa Verde
items.notes: Estimated carbohydrate: Qdoba's August 2026 guide publishes 10 calories, 0 g total carbohydrate, and 1 g dietary fiber, which is internally impossible. Two grams of carbohydrate best reconciles the calorie total while preserving at least 1 g fiber. Calories remain official. Medium confidence.
